content.text:
**Observations**

*Untrained vs. trained weights.* Many W1 rows have all 16 values inside ±0.036 with no spatial coherence – that is exactly the uniform initialisation range for fan‑in 784 (±1/√784 ≈ 0.036). These rows mark pixels that were essentially always 0 in training (zero gradient). Their layout is:
- Row 0: everything is init‑noise except columns 12–13 (which carry weights up to 0.10).
- Row 1: columns 0–3 and 24–27 are noise, columns 4–23 are clearly trained (0.1–0.2).
- Row 2: columns 0–2 and 26–27 noise, columns 3–25 trained, with very large values (unit 1 +0.30, unit 10 −0.40, unit 8 +0.33) at columns 6–10.
- Rows 23–27: only columns 0–1(2) and 26–27 are noise; row 27 is trained from column 4 to 23 with large weights (unit 2 down to −0.335, unit 14 +0.28, unit 15 −0.25).
- Left edge: columns 2–4 at rows 4–16 carry a very consistent, strong signature (unit 10 ≈ +0.2…+0.3, unit 5 +0.2…+0.3, unit 14 +0.2, unit 6 ≈ −0.15…−0.2); it sits at col 4–6 in row 4, col 3 in row 6 and col 2 in rows 7–11, i.e. it traces a diagonal contour running outward and down from the top.
- Right edge: column 26 (rows 10–15) and columns 23–26 (rows 23–25) hold the largest weights in the whole matrix (|w| up to 0.38), with units 0, 2, 6, 8, 10, 12 negative and units 7, 8, 11, 15 positive.
So the “always blank” set is only the four corners; content reaches the very top (but only at the horizontal centre), the full bottom row over a ~20‑pixel span, and both lateral edges in the middle rows.

*Hidden units.* Unit 1: positive over the whole top band (rows 1–3), negative at mid‑left (rows 15–17, cols 5–9) and bottom‑right (rows 25–26, cols 20–24) → “top‑heavy object”. Unit 10: negative on the upper‑left shoulder area (rows 1–2, cols 4–10), positive along the diagonal left contour (rows 4–11, cols 2–6) and along the bottom row → “sloping shoulders / low wide object”. Unit 2: a broad negative band across rows 6–9, cols 9–21, negative along the entire bottom row, positive at rows 12–16, cols 7–13. Unit 0: a solid positive patch at rows 11–14, cols 15–23 (middle of the frame) and strong negatives at the right edge. Unit 9: positive at the top band and bottom rows, negative in the centre at rows 5–8 and row 23. These are large, smooth, blob/outline‑shaped receptive fields, not thin stroke detectors.

*Output layer.* W2 is dense, |w| up to ~1.5. Unit 1 pushes classes 0, 1, 2, 6 up and 4, 5, 8, 9 down; unit 2 pushes 4 and 6 up and 8, 9 down; unit 9 separates class 7 (+1.22) from 5 (−0.52); unit 15 separates 5 (+0.61) from 9 (−1.32); unit 6 separates 1 (+1.22) from 3 (−1.24) and 2 (−1.00); unit 4 is strongly anti‑1 and anti‑3. Classes {5,7,9} and {0,2,4,6} repeatedly appear as the pairs a unit has to tease apart, suggesting two families of visually similar classes.

**Reasoning**

- MNIST / EMNIST are excluded: their digits/letters sit in a centred 20×20 box, so rows 0–3, 24–27 and the outer columns are always blank and would stay at init noise. Here rows 1–2 and 26–27 carry some of the largest weights in the network, and the lateral edge columns are heavily used.
- The blank mask is exactly "corners only": objects fill the frame edge‑to‑edge both vertically (tall objects touching rows 0 and 27) and horizontally (wide objects touching columns 0–2 / 25–27 in the middle rows). That is the signature of a dataset where each object is rescaled so its longest side spans the 28 pixels and is centred – Fashion‑MNIST's preprocessing.
- The top row is active only at the horizontal centre (collar / neckline / dress straps / bag handles are the highest point), while the bottom row is active over columns 4–23 (hems of shirts, trousers, dresses are wide). Hand‑written characters (KMNIST) would give roughly symmetric, narrow top and bottom activity and stroke‑like interior filters, not a narrow‑top/wide‑bottom silhouette.
- The diagonal left‑edge contour feature (unit 10) running from (4,5) down to (11,2) is a shoulder‑to‑sleeve outline; the broad negative band across the upper torso in unit 2 and the solid mid‑frame patch in unit 0 are garment/bag silhouette features. Receptive fields are large filled regions rather than strokes – consistent with solid clothing shapes.
- The output layer's recurring confusable groups {0,2,4,6} (upper‑body garments: T‑shirt/pullover/coat/shirt) and {5,7,9} (footwear: sandal/sneaker/ankle boot), with units dedicated to sneaker‑vs‑sandal and sandal‑vs‑boot, match the well‑known confusion structure of Fashion‑MNIST.

**Dataset:** Fashion‑MNIST (Zalando clothing‑article images, 28×28 grayscale, 10 classes).

**Classes:** 0 T‑shirt/top, 1 Trouser, 2 Pullover, 3 Dress, 4 Coat, 5 Sandal, 6 Shirt, 7 Sneaker, 8 Bag, 9 Ankle boot.

**Confidence:** 72%
